items.title: Recyclable Triboelectric Nanogenerators Enabled by Biodegradable Pollen‐Paper Nanoarchitectonics for Sustainable Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising devices for harvesting ambient mechanical energy, however, their development is hindered by low power output, limited energy conversion efficiency, and reliance on synthetic polymers. Here, we report a pollen‐based recyclable TENG (PRTENG) achieving a power density of 5.07 W m −2 , rivaling synthetic polymeric TENGs. The seamless integration of bleached pollen paper with PEDOT:PSS and poly(vinyl alcohol) via strong hydrogen‐bonding networks exhibits a 21% increase in maximum stress and 82‐fold toughness enhancement alongside robust durability of over 100 000 contact‐separation cycles. Moreover, when integrated into footwear, the PRTENG effectively converts human motion into electrical energy. Critically, water‐assisted disassembly enables complete component recovery for reassembly with negligible performance loss, while the recovered substrates can biodegrade within 12 days. Overall, this study provides a sustainable approach to engineer fully flexible, recyclable, and eco‐friendly TENGs for deployment in wearable electronics, decentralized sensing networks, and next‐generation sustainable IoT infrastructures.

items.title: Nanofiller-Enhanced Polar Beta (β)-Phase formation in PVDF Composites: A Mini Review of System for Application in Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: Renewable, Convenient, and Sustainable energy has emerged as the developmental trend for electronic devices and portable electronics, which are prevalent in our daily life. Most electronic devices must exhibit lightweight characteristics, strong conductivity, elevated dielectric permittivity, minimal dielectric loss, and substantial breakdown strength. Consequently, polymer-based piezoelectric materials are in high demand for the design and development of energy storage and sensing applications. Among the piezoelectric polymer, poly (vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) with a mainly polar β-Phase is the most remarkable. However, the main drawbacks of the PVDF matrix are its relatively low electrical conductivity and poor harvesting and low sensing performances. In this study, the incorporation of nanoparticles in the PVDF matrix has synergistic increases electro-active β- phase due to of their unique properties. Here we have reviewed the formation process of the polar β-Phase in PVDF matrix and PVDF piezoelectric properties related to energy harvesting and sensing application.

items.title: Dual-band terahertz refractive index sensor based on chiral metasurface
items.abstract: Abstract Metasurface sensor has become one of the emerging technologies in the field of micro and nano photonics in recent years. Chiral metasurface has unique advantages in chiral molecular detection and biosensing. This paper proposes a terahertz refractive index sensor based on chiral metasurface, which consists of a top layer of pattern, a dielectric layer and a bottom layer of metal reflection layer. The simulation results show that the maximum difference of circular dichroism (CD) spectra reaches 0.8 and -0.76 at 6.51 THz and 6.99 THz, respectively.The sensitivities of refractive index reach -1.04 THz/RIU and -1.093 THz/RIU respectively at two peaks. Therefore, the proposed metasurface sensor using chiral sensing method has the advantages of high sensitivity and wide range of refractive index detection. The sensor can be extended to industrial fields such as terahertz biological and chemical sensing.

items.title: Differential rotational and translational movements along the thoraco-lumbo-sacral spine of load and non-load pulling military and police horses walking and trotting on hard and soft surfaces
items.abstract: Abstract To improve detection of equine back-related disorders, it is important to establish how movement dynamics in horses’ thoraco-lumbo-sacral spine are normally affected by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. This cross-sectional study aimed to quantify how discipline, gait, and surface impact differential rotational and translational movements along the backs of 107 horses from the military and police forces. The horses were walked and trotted in-hand in a straight-line over hard and soft surfaces. During the exercises, nine inertial sensors (XSens MTw) were mounted to the poll, withers, thoracic vertebrae-13 (T13) and 18 (T18), lumbar vertebra-3 (L3), sacrum (between tubera sacrale), left and right tubera coxae, and caudal sacrum (‘tail’). Linear mixed models assessed whether horse discipline (load pulling or non-load pulling), surface (soft or hard), age, or stride time influenced rotational and translational range of motion differences between adjacent sensors at either walk or trot (significance at p < 0.05). When compared to non-load pullers, it was apparent that the load pullers had reductions in differential rotational movements (0.5–3.1º in walk, p ≤ 0.039; and 0.5–2.3º in trot, p ≤ 0.049) and reductions in differential cranio-caudal, medio-lateral and dorso-ventral translations (2.2–15.0 mm in walk, p ≤ 0.039; and 1.2–7.6 mm, p ≤ 0.045 in trot), plus an increase in differential cranio-caudal translation at the Poll-Withers (12.8 mm in trot, p < 0.001). Soft surfaces increased differential rotational movements (0.1–1.2º in walk, p ≤ 0.048; and 0.2–2.9º in trot, p ≤ 0.007) and differential translational movements (1.4–16.3 mm in walk, p ≤ 0.002; and 0.5–2 mm in trot, p ≤ 0.007) in most regions of the thoraco-lumbo-sacral spine compared to hard surfaces. The amplitude of differential rotational and translational movements did not show systematic patterns with stride time and age. Further work is needed to understand whether the observed changes to differential rotational and translational movements along the equine thoraco-lumbo-sacral spine, imposed by working discipline and surface conditions, impact long-term equine health, well-being, or susceptibility to injury. This work will lay foundations for the development of an equine back dynamics reference framework, to which individual data may be compared.

items.title: A vision-based tactile sensor with in-sensor computing paradigm for seamless tactile sensing and perception
items.abstract: Abstract Vision-based tactile sensors (VBTSs) offer high-resolution, multimodal tactile sensing capabilities, supporting precise and dexterous robotic manipulation. However, the physical separation of sensing and perception modules necessitates frequent data transfer, introducing communication overhead and potentially constraining real-time performance. In biological tactile systems, sensory transduction and preliminary signal processing occur at the periphery before information is transmitted to the central nervous system, thereby enabling efficient and timely tactile perception. Inspired by this principle, we present PixelTac, a VBTS designed under an in-sensor computing paradigm. PixelTac integrates sensing, memory, and computation within a single in-situ vision processor that combines a computational pixel matrix and a microcontroller. This architecture enables local compression of tactile data and fully on-chip processing from pixel-level sensing to force inference. Here, we show that PixelTac reproduces key features of human mechanoreception in real-time while maintaining efficient power consumption, providing a scalable and energy-efficient route to seamless tactile sensing and perception.

items.title: Formal polarization as a Quantized Bulk Invariant: Implications for Interface Phenomena
items.abstract: Abstract In crystalline solids, symmetry can constrain formal polarization to discrete values. We show that this quantized formal polarization (QFP) should be understood as a symmetry-protected bulk invariant that encodes intrinsic information about a material’s symmetry and electronic structure. From this viewpoint, mismatch between the QFPs of different materials or phases represents a bulk incompatibility with potentially broad physical consequences. In particular, when such materials form an interface, the QFP mismatch imposes a nontrivial compensation requirement, which may be realized through metallic states, bound charges, structural reconstructions, or other mechanisms. Through the examples of the ZnS/MgS heterostructure, the HfZnN 2 domain wall, and the GaAs domain wall, we demonstrate that bulk QFP provides a predictive criterion for determining whether nontrivial interfacial compensation is required, without explicitly constructing the interface or domain wall. The specific realization of this compensation, however, must be determined from explicit calculations for each material system. Our work thus elevates formal polarization from a quantity used mainly in interface electrostatics to a more general bulk principle relevant to phase compatibility and related phenomena, and suggests a route toward designing functional quantum materials through controlled quantized polarization mismatch.

items.title: Characterizing high pathogenicity island in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae : regulations, functions, and modulation methods
items.abstract:
Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) is emerging as an important pathogen of concern that causes invasive diseases and multidrug resistance worldwide. Many hvKp strains carry a high-pathogenicity island (HPI), a horizontally acquired genomic locus that frequently encodes the siderophore yersiniabactin (ybt) in combination with the genotoxin colibactin (pks). How HPI is regulated, what host responses it elicits, and whether it can be therapeutically exploited remain incompletely understood in hvKp. This thesis aims to contribute new knowledge to these questions through three complementary studies in SGH4, a sequence type 23 hvKp isolate using bacterial transcriptional reporters, host infection models and iron-targeting antimicrobial materials.

First, a dual-fluorescent transcriptional reporter system pGERC was developed to enable simultaneous monitoring of two HPI genes' promoter activity in real time. This system revealed coordinated, growth-phase-dependent and iron-responsive expression of the colibactin and yersiniabactin loci, while also identifying regulatory features in SGH4 that differ from models established in pks-positive E. coli. Second, in animal and cellular infection models, hvKp colibactin was shown to induce persistent DNA damage and consequently activate cGAS-STING-TBK1-dependent type I interferon responses. In mice, pks-positive SGH4 persisted in the intestine and induced DNA damage at the colonic crypt surface, whereas a colibactin-deficient mutant was rapidly cleared. Third, gallium phosphate nanoparticles were evaluated as an iron-mimetic antibacterial approach based on the observations made in part I and II. Although they did not inhibit hvKp growth, they suppressed planktonic growth, biofilm formation, pyoverdine production, and bacterial burden of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the lung.

Together, these studies define non-canonical regulatory features of the hvKp HPI, identify colibactin-linked innate immune activation during host interaction, and explore the opportunities and limitations of targeting bacterial iron metabolism as an antibacterial strategy.

items.title: Unveiling Affective Polarization Trends in Parliamentary Proceedings
items.abstract: Abstract Recent years have seen an increase in polarized discourse worldwide, on various platforms. We propose a novel method for quantifying polarization, based on the emotional style of the discourse rather than on differences in ideological stands. Using measures of Valence, Arousal, and Dominance, we detect signals of emotional discourse and use them to operationalize the concept of affective polarization. Applying this method to a recently released corpus of proceedings of the Knesset, the Israeli parliament (in Hebrew), we find that the emotional style of members of government differs from that of opposition members; and that the level of affective polarization, as reflected by this style, is significantly increasing with time.

items.title: Universal modulation of liquid-liquid phase separation by macromolecules
items.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) widely organizes the cellular interior, yet how third-party macromolecules modulate LLPS remains a puzzle. While one would expect that macromolecules can either promote or suppress phase separation, empirical observations show that a small dosage of macromolecules virtually always promotes phase separation. To resolve this paradox, we study the linear response of phase separation to macromolecule addition. We prove that for macromolecules significantly larger than the solvent molecule, their addition essentially always promotes phase separation, regardless of how they interact with the scaffold protein. Crucially, in the biologically relevant scenario of dilute condensates, the linear responses, including the saturation volume fraction, scale proportionally to [1-v 2 (1+χ 12 ) 2 ], where v 2 is the macromolecule size and χ 12 is the scaffold-macromolecule interaction parameter. Importantly, this universal behavior extends to multicomponent solutions in which the effective interaction parameter is composition-dependent. Our work shifts macromolecular modulation of LLPS from empirical observation to predictable design.

items.title: Photography between Moulding and Modulation
items.abstract: This article rethinks photography through Gilbert Simondon’s distinction between moulding and modulation. While photography has long been theorised as a moulding medium – an instantaneous imprint of reality, a decisive moment fixed in time – it is equally constituted by processes of modulation: continuous adjustments of exposure, development, calibration and computation. Drawing on examples from nineteenth-century composite printing to contemporary computational and synthetic photography, the article shows that moulding and modulation are not historical stages or rival media, but heuristic poles that illuminate the technical dynamics of photographic individuation. Photography, the article argues, is best understood as a parameter-image: a field of potential variation that continually modulates the very concept of what photography is.

items.title: Emergence of Lissajous trajectories in a skyrmion oscillator
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the dynamics of current-driven skyrmions is essential for their practical applications. In this study, we apply an ac pulse (a) in the x -direction, and (b) in both x -and y -directions through the free layer of a Co/Pt thin film and investigate the motion of the skyrmion. We show that the skyrmion follows a sinusoidal current pulse and behaves like an oscillator in the range of current amplitude 1 × 10 11 A m − 2 –1 × 10 12 A m − 2 and frequency 5 × 10 8 rad s − 1 –1 × 10 10 rad s − 1 . For current pulses of ( A 1 sin ω 1 t, A 2 sin( ω 2 t+ ϕ ), 0), the skyrmion forms Lissajous figures in the x – y plane, same as observed in classical mechanics. The results are compared at T = 0 K and T > 0 K to analyze the effect of temperature. As the skyrmion Hall angle ( θ SkH ) and stochastic thermal fluctuation ( F Th ) are functions of temperature, the skyrmion starts deviating from its path at T = 0 K with increasing temperature and eventually generates somewhat deformed Lissajous figures from the ideal.

items.title: Centrosome migration and apical membrane formation during epithelial polarization in MDCK cysts
items.abstract: Polarization is crucial for the proper functioning of epithelial cells. Early hallmarks include the trafficking and enrichment of polarity molecules to form the apical membrane (AM) or cell–cell junctions, and the apical positioning of the centrosome. However, the dependencies among polarity molecules, AM formation, and centrosome positioning remain poorly understood. When cultured in Matrigel, de novo polarization of a single epithelial cell is often coupled with cytokinesis. During mitotic exit, centrosomes move to the future AM site, raising questions about their role in polarization. We perturbed centrosomes and polarity regulators in Matrigel-cultured cells and manipulated polarity direction using suspension culture to examine the relationships among polarization features. Surprisingly, centrosomal microtubules may not be necessary for centrosome positioning or AM formation, but their absence reduces the efficiency of AM formation. The polarity regulator Par3, rather than AM component trafficking, influences centrosome positioning. In suspension culture, centrosomes migrate in the direction opposite to AM formation. Taken together, our findings define the hierarchical relationships among several polarization features and show that centrosome-based polarity is not universal in epithelial cells, providing new insights into the mechanisms of epithelial polarization.

items.title: Biomimetic Olfactory System Based on Temperature-Modulated Sensor Arrays for Detecting Trace Volatile Semiochemicals of Plants
items.abstract: Abstract Volatile aroma compounds (VACs) are key semiochemicals induced and released by plants under biotic and abiotic stresses. Therefore, it is of great significance for detecting VACs to evaluate the growth environment information and physiological markers of plants. However, real-time and on-site monitoring of VACs at the current stage remains a challenge due to their complex species and trace concentrations. Here, we report an ultrasensitive VAC sensor based on Ru-nanocluster-anchored ZnO nanodisks, for which the corresponding limit of detection for VACs can reach as low as 10 ppb. By constructing temperature-modulated 4 × 4 VAC sensor arrays and integrating artificial intelligence algorithms, we demonstrate simultaneous identification of 10 VAC species and concentrations with 98% accuracy and high fidelity. Furthermore, a portable biomimetic olfactory e-nose based on temperature-modulated sensor arrays was developed to realize the on-site detection of VACs released from tea plants induced by Ectropis obliqua. This work not only provides a design strategy for ultrasensitive VAC sensors but also establishes a scalable platform for real-time plant health monitoring and early warning of biotic and abiotic stresses.

items.title: A Compact Coupled-Line Butterworth Bandpass Filter for Sub-6 GHz Applications
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and experimental validation of a compact microstrip bandpass filter operating at 3.5 GHz for sub-6 GHz 5G wireless communication systems. The proposed filter is realized using a fourth-order Butterworth response implemented through a parallel coupled-line topology, aiming to achieve a maximally flat passband response, low insertion loss, and sufficient selectivity within the n77 frequency band (3.3-3.8 GHz). The design procedure starts with the synthesis of a normalized low-pass Butterworth prototype, followed by bandpass transformation and its implementation as an equivalent distributed microstrip structure. Electromagnetic analysis and parametric optimization are employed to accurately model coupling effects, transmission line behavior, and fabrication constraints. The filter is fabricated on a low-cost FR-4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.3 and a thickness of 0.8 mm using standard printed circuit board manufacturing techniques. Experimental characterization is performed using a vector network analyzer to evaluate the frequency response. Measurement results demonstrate a center frequency of 3.5 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of approximately 300 MHz, showing good agreement with the predicted performance. The proposed bandpass filter offers a compact footprint, simple geometry, and reliable frequency response, making it a suitable candidate for integration into 5G radio-frequency front-end modules and other modern wireless communication systems.

items.title: Design of composite control strategy for improving the tracking effect of permanent magnet synchronous wind power generation system
items.abstract: This article proposes a composite control strategy system to address the issue of wind speed tracking performance without position sensors in the operation of permanent magnet synchronous wind power generation systems within complex environments. The speed loop control module of this strategy employs a refined active disturbance rejection control (RADRC) strategy as its core, supplemented by a parallel proportional integral (PI) controller to enhance speed loop control, efficiently suppressing external disturbances like wind speed fluctuations and improving speed control accuracy and steady-state performance. By introducing an additional compensation term into its internal model to alleviate the influence of estimation lag, the RADRC strategy is capable of achieving faster and more accurate estimation performance. Meanwhile, active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) technology is applied in the current loop control, with a parallel PI controller to significantly boost transient response and anti-disturbance robustness. The speed observer utilizes an improved model reference adaptive system (MRAS), where the adaptive law is mainly based on a PI controller, with a parallel ADRC regulator introduced to further reduce speed estimation errors. Compared with conventional PI or ADRC based adaptive strategies, the proposed observer achieves more accurate rotor speed estimation and improves the dynamic response of the system. In the design process, the mathematical model system of the permanent magnet synchronous wind power generation system is first established, and a comprehensive theoretical analysis is carried out on the proposed composite control strategy. Then, based on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform, a system simulation model is constructed to verify control strategies under various typical wind speed conditions. Simulation experimental data shows that compared to traditional control schemes, adopting this composite control strategy significantly enhances operational stability.

items.title: Accuracy, precision, and efficiency of manual planimetry versus point counting for sectional area estimation in oral morphometry: a comparison using a simulated two-dimensional reference model
items.abstract: Background Reliable sectional area measurement is essential for quantitative analysis in dental imaging, histomorphometry, and guided surgery. Although manual planimetry and point counting are widely used, their comparative measurement performance at the isolated two-dimensional level has seldom been evaluated against a predefined nominal reference. Materials and methods A simulated two-dimensional nominal reference model was created using 30 artificial sections with mathematically predefined true areas. Two observers independently measured the area of each section with both methods; all measurements were repeated after a two-week washout period. For each method, repeatability, absolute bias relative to the true area, and time required per section were evaluated. Bland–Altman analysis was used to characterize the structural patterns of measurement error. Results Both methods showed excellent repeatability. However, point counting yielded a significantly smaller average bias and required less time per section than manual planimetry. Bland–Altman analysis revealed distinct error profiles: manual planimetry was characterized by systematic underestimation that increased with section size and geometric complexity, whereas point counting maintained consistent accuracy across the entire range of section areas. Conclusions Under the controlled two-dimensional workflows tested, point counting showed smaller bias and greater efficiency than manual planimetry. However, because planimetry was performed on scanned images whereas point counting was performed directly on physical sections, these findings should be interpreted as a comparison of the tested implementations rather than evidence of intrinsic methodological superiority. Manual planimetry, although highly repeatable, was susceptible to systematic underestimation, particularly when delineating complex and fragmented contours. These findings may inform methodological selection in morphometric studies, but their relevance to automated segmentation evaluation requires further validation in clinical or histological datasets.

items.title: The prognostic nutritional index vs. MELD for short-term mortality in critically ill liver disease: a retrospective multi-cohort study
items.abstract: Malnutrition, sarcopenia and frailty are common in advanced liver disease and predict poorer survival, encouraging simple blood-based indices when formal assessment is impractical. The most widely used, the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI), combines serum albumin and the peripheral lymphocyte count; yet both have been reported to be strongly influenced by systemic inflammation as well as by nutrition, and the index is seldom benchmarked against a disease-specific reference or against albumin alone. We evaluated whether the PNI provides clinically useful prognostic information for short-term mortality in critically ill patients with liver disease, using three independent cohorts: a North American intensive-care primary cohort ( n = 3,653), a multicentre external-validation cohort ( n = 922) and a single-center Chinese cohort in which hepatitis B was the leading cause of liver disease ( n = 453). In each cohort we quantified discrimination of 28-day or in-hospital mortality, compared the PNI with serum albumin alone and with the Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD), and tested whether it improved discrimination or reclassification beyond MELD. The PNI discriminated death only marginally better than chance (area under the curve 0.52–0.56) and no better than albumin alone, so its lymphocyte component added no independent signal; the weak per-standard-deviation association seen in the primary cohort was not significant in either validation cohort. MELD discriminated substantially better everywhere (0.67–0.70). The conventional PNI threshold classified 89–97% of patients as abnormal and was uninformative. Across three case-mixes the PNI behaved as a weak, non-specific prognostic discriminator, adding nothing to MELD, MELD-Na or MELD 3.0; in an exploratory paired subgroup, re-measurement on days 3–7 did not improve discrimination. This is consistent with its components tracking systemic inflammation and chronic physiologic reserve—an axis largely orthogonal to the acute organ failure that drives short-term mortality. Separating the index into its components and testing incremental value provides the comparative evidence this literature has lacked. The PNI was assessed as a discriminator of short-term mortality, not as a measure of nutritional status: nutritional risk is better identified with instruments validated for that purpose, and mortality risk with MELD.

items.title: Effect of solution pH and concentration of Dewandaru fruit extract as a natural dye on optical characteristics and performance of dye-sensitized solar cells
items.venue: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development
items.abstract: Given growing global energy demand and the need for sustainable solutions, solar energy is a promising alternative. Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSC) are a cost-effective photovoltaic technology, and natural dyes as sensitizers have significant potential to improve their efficiency. This study explores the use of a natural dye from the Dewandaru fruit (Eugenia uniflora) in DSSCs by varying pH and concentration. Natural dyes offer an environmentally friendly, sustainable alternative to synthetic dyes, which are often expensive and less eco-friendly. In this research, Dewandaru fruit extract was used to sensitize TiO2 photoanodes, and the effects of varying pH (1.00, 1.66, 2.27, and 3.00) and dye concentrations (2.5, 5.0, 7.5, and 10%) on optical properties and performance were analyzed. UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, cyclic voltammetry, and J-V measurements were used to assess absorbance, energy levels, and efficiency. Optical characterization results showed that changes in pH and concentration can affect the dye’s absorbance and energy band gap. The dye achieved optimal DSSC performance at pH 3.00, yielding a Voc of 0.425 V, Jsc of 0.053 mA/cm², a fill factor of 68.7%, and an efficiency of 0.01548%. The best dye concentration was 10%, achieving a Voc of 0.45 V, a Jsc of 0.105 mA/cm², a fill factor of 69.0%, and an efficiency of 0.0322%. The statistical analysis indicates that pH has a substantial positive effect on DSSC efficiency and band gap energy. Moreover, dye concentration significantly affects DSSC efficiency, light-harvesting efficiency, Jsc, and fill factor, with the most substantial effects on efficiency and Jsc. However, concentration appears to have a smaller effect on dye absorbance, band gap energy, and HOMO/LUMO values. The study indicates that Dewandaru fruit extract has potential as a natural dye for DSSCs, with performance varying with pH and concentration.

items.title: Modeling a 5D Hamiltonian conservative hyperchaotic oscillator with complicated dynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Based on the 3D Euler equation, 5D generalized Euler equations are realized by introducing three coupling parameters and combining three subbodies with two same axes, whose Casimir energy and Hamiltonian are both conservative. By violating the Casimir energy conservation, a 5D Hamiltonian hyperchaotic oscillator is postulated. Through nonlinear analysis methods, it is found that the 5D Hamiltonian conservative hyperchaotic system possesses complicated dynamic behaviors, such as a wide constant range, hidden chaotic orbit, bursting oscillation, transient bursting, and multi-orbit coexistence. Then, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) statistical test suite is employed to evaluate the randomness quality of the pseudo-random sequences generated by the system, indicating their potential suitability for chaos-based cryptographic applications. Finally, the physical feasibility of the oscillator is validated through both analog circuit simulation and STM32-based hardware implementation.

items.title: A TRANSFORMERLESS HIGH-GAIN DC-DC CONVERTER FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE APPLICATIONS
items.venue: REVUE ROUMAINE DES SCIENCES TECHNIQUES — SÉRIE ÉLECTROTECHNIQUE ET ÉNERGÉTIQUE
items.abstract: Reliable DC power is essential for the continuous operation of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in EV systems. Since these systems require a specific voltage level that many sources cannot directly provide, an efficient voltage-boosting stage is necessary. This paper presents a higher-voltage-gain structure for a non-isolated DC/DC converter with a switched-inductor-based double-switch configuration to step up a low input voltage to a stable high output suitable for EV applications. The proposed converter is analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate voltage gain, efficiency, and device stresses. A 100 W hardware prototype producing 200 V output is developed for validation. Both simulation and experimental results confirm improved voltage regulation and reduced output ripple under varying duty conditions. Overall, the topology provides a practical and efficient solution for EV battery energy storage systems.

items.title: Physics-Informed Dual-View YOLO Framework for Tennis Ball Trajectory Prediction
items.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Abstract The flight behavior of spinning tennis balls constitutes a nonlinear aerodynamic system governed by the coupling among translational motion, rotational dynamics, gravity, and aerodynamic forces. Conventional trajectory prediction methods often rely on simplified projectile assumptions and therefore fail to accurately reconstruct spin-induced nonlinear trajectory evolution under realistic high-speed sports conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physics-informed tennis trajectory reconstruction framework integrating synchronized dual-view motion acquisition, YOLO-based object localization, three-dimensional kinematic reconstruction, and Magnus-effect-informed aerodynamic simulation. Side-view and top-view observations are utilized to estimate key motion parameters, including initial velocity, elevation angle, and lateral motion angle, which are subsequently incorporated into a nonlinear aerodynamic trajectory model considering gravity, drag, and spin-induced lift forces. Experiments were conducted using 40 tennis strokes collected under daytime and nighttime conditions on a red clay court with physically measured landing-point references. The results demonstrate that incorporating Magnus-effect coupling substantially improves longitudinal trajectory reconstruction accuracy. Specifically, the Z-axis mean absolute error decreased from 2.49 m to 1.08 m, while the overall RMSE decreased from 2.82 m to 1.52 m compared with the non-Magnus model. Spatial deviation analysis further revealed reduced systematic prediction bias and improved trajectory stability under varying illumination conditions. The proposed framework establishes a coupled visual–physical paradigm for nonlinear sports trajectory reconstruction by integrating deep learning–based motion acquisition with physics-informed aerodynamic modeling. The study contributes toward physically consistent landing-point prediction, intelligent sports analytics, and high-fidelity trajectory simulation in high-speed sports environments.

items.title: Improved efficiency for better resolved solid-state NMR studies of Aluminum sites in materials
items.abstract: In solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy of materials, a multiple-quantum magic angle spinning (MQMAS) experiment is routinely employed to characterize quadrupolar nuclei. It provides high-resolution isotropic spectra correlated with anisotropic quadrupolar lineshapes that contain valuable structural information. For aluminum (27Al, spin 5/2), a key constituent of active catalytic sites in zeolites, quintuple-quantum magic angle spinning (5QMAS) NMR spectroscopy provides substantially increased frequency dispersion in the isotropic dimension relative to its conventional triple-quantum (3QMAS) counterpart. However, the enhanced resolution of 5QMAS remains largely underexplored due to prohibitively low sensitivity for most samples. To overcome this limitation, optimal control (OC) method was used to design highly efficient excitation and reconversion pulses for both 3QMAS and 5QMAS sequences. Using Al(acac)3 reference sample, experimental 3QMAS and 5QMAS spectra acquired with specifically tailored OC pulses yielded 3.4- and 18.5-fold higher signal intensities relative to conventional rectangular pulses, respectively, at magnetic field strength of 9.4 T and MAS frequency of 12.5 kHz. Analogous measurements conducted at 14.1 T and MAS frequency of 55.555 kHz provided corresponding signal enhancements of 5.2- and 50-fold. Although broadband OC pulses optimized over broader distributions of quadrupolar coupling parameters and chemical shifts exhibit lower relative signal enhancements, OC-5QMAS for a hydrated MFI zeolite sample yielded a 6-fold intensity enhancement relative to the conventional 5QMAS experiment. Furthermore, the OC-5QMAS spectra exhibited a signal-to-noise ratio superior to that of traditional 3QMAS spectra, thereby enabling routine 27Al solid-state NMR characterization of tetrahedral sites with both improved sensitivity and larger frequency dispersion to potentially resolve crystallographically distinct framework positions.

items.title: Economic Efficiency and Productivity of Smallholder Teff Producers in Awabel District of East Gojjam Zone in Ethiopia
items.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Abstract Improving agricultural resource-use efficiency is essential for advancing sustainable food systems, reducing rural poverty, and strengthening the contribution of smallholder agriculture to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production). In Ethiopia, where despite the profound cultural, nutritional, and economic dominance of teff(Eragrostis tef), farm-level productivity faces major structural bottlenecks within the East Gojjam Zone. This study investigates the technical, allocative, and overall economic efficiencies among smallholder teff farmers in Awabel District, East Gojjam zone, as well as their underlying socio-economic and institutional determinants.A two-stage stratified random sampling technique was used to survey 360 target household heads across various agro-ecological strata. By employing a parametric Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA) framework to isolate manageable internal inefficiencies from random environmental noise, the econometric results show that teff cultivation operates under decreasing returns to scale, with cultivated land size emerging as the dominant frontier driver of output expansion.Yields are greatly and favorably impacted by both contemporary materials like chemical fertilizers and pesticides as well as inputs like labor and oxen. Ultimately, the mean technical, allocative, and economic efficiency scores are estimated at 82.45%, 75.63%, and 63.79%, respectively, showing that structural cost distortions and allocative failures represent the primary barriers to financial optimization. Inefficiency modeling shows that formal education, practical farming experience, extension contacts, targeted training, microcredit access, livestock holdings, and favorable weather conditions significantly minimize economic inefficiency. Policymakers should concentrate on stabilizing localized land rental registries, expanding credit mechanisms to address seasonal cash starvation, and shifting public extension networks toward management-capacity building.

items.title: Dielectric barrier discharge cold plasma inactivation of Ephestia kuehniella and quality assessment of wheat flour
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effectiveness of cold dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma for controlling different developmental stages of the Mediterranean flour moth ( Ephestia kuehniella) in wheat flour. Eggs, larvae, and pupae were treated under different voltage and exposure time combinations using a dual power supply DBD system. Each treatment was performed with five replicates. Plasma treatment showed clear stage-dependent efficacy. The optimum treatment reduced adult emergence from eggs by approximately 88%, whereas larvae were the most susceptible stage, exhibiting nearly 100% mortality at 19 kV after 5–9 min of treatment. Larval mortality continued to increase during the 10-day post-treatment period. Pupae were the most tolerant stage, with the greatest suppression of adult emergence achieved at 24 kV for 13 min. To determine whether insecticidal treatments affected the commodity, selected physicochemical properties of wheat flour were evaluated. Color measurements revealed only minor changes (ΔE = 1.05 ± 0.83). SEM observations showed slight qualitative surface modifications, while ATR-FTIR analysis indicated limited chemical changes consistent with oxidation. Overall, the results demonstrate stage-dependent insecticidal efficacy of atmospheric DBD plasma with only limited physicochemical modifications to wheat flour under the conditions evaluated.

items.title: Pixel-Level autonomous identification method for self-explosion defects of aerial insulators based on Deep Q-Network and reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Visible light inspection of insulators by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) often suffers from image degradation caused by interference such as illumination, vegetation and atmospheric conditions. Conventional detection methods can only realize fault detection, and fail to conduct pixel-level quantitative measurement of damaged areas. To address this problem, a pixel-level autonomous identification method for self-explosion defects of UAV aerial insulators based on Deep Q-Network (DQN) and reinforcement learning is proposed. Dark channel dehazing and bilateral edge-preserving denoising are integrated to enhance insulator images. An accurate positioning and segmentation method for insulator strings based on the improved CV model is adopted. The inclination angle is calculated by combining the saliency of the blue channel of insulators and Hough transform, and an adaptive elliptical level set is constructed to extract the target regions of insulators in images. The segmented images are imported into the pixel-level autonomous identification model for insulator self-explosion defects built on DQN and reinforcement learning. Multi-scale features of self-explosion defects are extracted to generate coarse defect probability maps. Pixels with ambiguous boundaries in masks are screened to establish an interactive environment for DQN reinforcement learning. The Intersection over Union (IoU) of segmentation is taken as the reward to dynamically adjust pixel thresholds and optimize defect contours. The corrected probabilities are fused to generate binary defect masks, the damaged area is converted, and pixel-level identification of defects is realized. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve pixel-level autonomous identification of insulator self-explosion defects and output accurate quantified damage sizes under high-interference field working conditions. It can provide reliable quantitative data support for refined fault grading and operation maintenance of transmission lines.

items.title: Mesoporous Bimetallic MOF for Efficient Mechanical Energy Harvesting in PVDF
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible mechanical energy harvesting using poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is a promising route toward self-powered wearable and IoT systems. However, the limited electroactive phase content of pristine PVDF restricts its performance. In this work, we investigate the influence of Co-, Ni-, and CoNi-metal−organic framework (MOF) fillers on the electromechanical properties of PVDF. Monometallic Co- and Ni-based MOFs and a bimetallic CoNi-MOF with a benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate linker were synthesized and incorporated into PVDF to form flexible composite films. Owing to its highly exfoliated 2D morphology, large accessible surface area, favorable mesoporous structure, and possible bimetallic synergy, the CoNi-MOF enables strong interfacial coupling with PVDF chains, leading to a substantial enhancement of electroactive phases. An optimal CoNi-MOF loading of 3 wt % in PVDF yields the highest polar phase fraction (∼88%) and a superior electromechanical response. Mechanical energy harvesters fabricated from this composite deliver an open-circuit voltage of ∼26 V, a short-circuit current of ∼7 μA, and a peak power density of ∼15 μW/cm2. The device further exhibits excellent dynamic and static pressure sensitivity, efficient capacitor charging, and effective harvesting of biomechanical energy from human motions. These results demonstrate that the investigated CoNi-MOF is an effective filler for high-performance PVDF-based mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing applications.

items.title: From Signals to Measurands: A Measurement-Science Roadmap for Reproducible Analytical Biochemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Analytical biochemistry often reports kinetic or binding constants as though they were observed directly. Each result is instead inferred from an instrumental signal. Calibration establishes the scale, biochemical and observation models connect the signal to a target, and statistical analysis produces the estimate and its uncertainty. This Perspective treats reproducibility as the recovery of a specified measurand, with an uncertainty statement, through an auditable measurement chain. A Michaelis–Menten substrate-depletion example provides the organizing case. Two progress-curve experiments generated with the same parameters and noise model both fit well, yet only the design that samples substrate concentrations around the Michaelis constant yields a bounded interval for KM. In that design, uncertainty in active-site concentration dominates the uncertainty of kcat even though the curve fit is precise. Ligand–receptor binding shows parallel effects of depletion, signal modeling, and parameter confounding. The framework connects established metrological and chemical-measurement concepts with enzymology reporting standards, machine-readable data formats, and modern identifiability analysis. It distinguishes repeatability, transfer to another laboratory, and agreement across independent measurement routes (or techniques), and explains what interlaboratory studies can reveal. The recommendations are prioritized as minimum practice, stronger support for parameter estimation, and reference-grade validation. The same logic applies whenever a biochemical quantity is inferred from a measured signal.

items.title: Dual-wavelength time-of-flight interferometric speckle-contrast optical spectroscopy (dual-wavelength TOF-iSCOS) for co-registered blood-flow and hemoglobin sensing
items.abstract: Diffuse optical measurements of blood flow, blood volume, and blood oxygenation often use separate devices and photon populations. Combining these contrasts within a common photon population would enable their direct co-registration while retaining time-of-flight-based depth discrimination. We introduce dual-wavelength time-of-flight interferometric speckle-contrast optical spectroscopy (TOF-iSCOS), built on an interferometric near-infrared spectroscopy (iNIRS) architecture that temporally multiplexes 780 and 852 nm swept lasers through a shared detection channel. It recovers co-registered flow-sensitive field dynamics and wavelength-resolved attenuation from the same complex-field acquisition. Three 50 ps TOF gates sample increasingly late-arriving photons. Within each gate, g_1 was calculated directly as the normalized temporal autocorrelation of the reconstructed complex field. κ2 was reconstructed by finite-time integration of measured g_1 and finite-integration fits yielded decorrelation rates. No camera speckle-variance contrast or Siegert substitution was used. Gate-integrated TPSF intensities yielded optical-density changes δOD, and division by the baseline-TPSF-weighted mean photon path length gave effective δμ_a for two-wavelength hemoglobin inversion. In 12 forearm cuff-occlusion recordings from 11 adults, TOF-iSCOS detected flow suppression during occlusion and reactive hyperemia after release at both wavelengths. At 780 nm, the Late-minus-Early reactive-hyperemia amplitude in the relative blood-flow index (rBFI) was +0.647 (95% CI 0.194 to 1.124), whereas the Early-minus-Late cuff δμ_a contrast was +0.196 cm^{-1} (95% CI 0.123 to 0.280). In the photon-limited 852 nm Late gate, the accepted-frame fraction was 0.994 for κ^2-based fitting versus 0.831 for g_1-based fitting. Exploratory phase-resolved analysis suggested that the initial hemoglobin response was concentrated in early-arriving photons, while later responses differed in magnitude and direction. Wavelength, field dynamics, and photon time-of-flight thus provide complementary physiological information; the largest response need not identify the phase of interest.

items.title: Comparative assessment of hydration status in intestinal failure patients receiving home parenteral nutrition using different bioimpedance analysis devices
items.abstract: abstract Background Intestinal failure patients receiving home parenteral nutrition (HPN) are at high risk of dehydration and malnutrition. To optimize clinical care, accurate monitoring tools are required. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of two bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) devices, one that offers only BIA results and the other that offers BIA results of bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA) and bioelectrical impedance spectroscopy (BIS), in assessing hydration and nutritional status in HPN patients. Patients and methods In a cross-sectional study, 55 adult HPN patients (33 males, 22 females; mean age 61.5 ±13.1 years) underwent BIA measurements using both devices during routine visits. Parameters measured included total body water (TBW), intracellular and extracellular water, fat-free mass, fat mass, and phase angle. Serum urea and creatinine served as hydration markers. Paired t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations were used for analysis. Results The BIA/BIVA/BIS analysis indicated dehydration in 69.1% of patients compared to 29.1% by BIA (p < 0.001) and showed stronger correlations with serum urea. It also classified more patients as malnourished (24.4% vs. 16.4%, p = 0.436). Correlation between hydration status and phase angle was more pronounced when using phase angle determined with BIA/BIVA/BIS. Conclusions BIA/BIVA/BIS measurements in the study demonstrated superior sensitivity in detecting dehydration and assessing nutritional status in HPN patients in comparison to BIA, supporting its use for improved clinical monitoring and management in this group of patients.

items.title: Archimedes‐Spiral Triboelectric Nanogenerator Based on Wave Height Amplifiers for Counter‐Phase Wave Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid–solid triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), owing to their high contact efficiency and structural simplicity, are regarded as a promising technological solution for wave energy harvesting. However, their performance is constrained by low spatial utilization efficiency and insufficient wave height under actual sea conditions. Herein, an Archimedes‐spiral triboelectric nanogenerator is constructed through a spiral integrated stacking design strategy, achieving a volumetric charge density of 29.19 mC·m −3 , a volumetric power density of 35.37 W·m −3 , and a triboelectric surface density of 5.55 cm −1 . A wave height amplifier scheme based on Bernoulli's principle and Pascal's law is proposed, which not only delivers a 2.4 fold amplification of wave height but also ensures compatibility with the TENG's internal motion. By constructing an external counter‐phase wave energy harvesting system, wave energy is transmitted to the inner TENG, thereby improving energy harvesting efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate that the device delivers high output charge quantity, voltage and current of 17.88 µC, 845 V, and 127 µA, respectively. Additionally, the device continuously powers two hygrothermographs and three calculators under simulated wave conditions, respectively, and also exhibits outstanding performance in real ocean environments. This study proposes a strategy to advance triboelectric nanogenerators for wave energy harvesting toward all‐weather applications.

items.title: An energy-based model empowers ultra-large virtual screening against 100-billion-scale chemical libraries
items.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Abstract Recent advances have expanded the accessible chemical space to nearly 100 billion molecules, offering unprecedented opportunities for discovering novel chemotypes in drug development. However, screening such vast libraries using conventional methods remains prohibitively expensive, thus inaccessible to most drug developers. To address this challenge, we propose DrugJEPA, an energy-based model that integrates contrastive learning with a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA). DrugJEPA achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on computational benchmarks. Furthermore, we construct a tailored virtual library of approximately 100 billion compounds (ZEUS-3D). Using this library, DrugJEPA completes a virtual screening campaign in just 28 hours on four GPUs—representing a speedup of up to seven orders of magnitude compared to molecular docking. In wet-laboratory validation experiments targeting three distinct protein classes (TYK2, TAAR1, and PUS1, representing kinase, GPCR, and epigenetic targets, respectively), DrugJEPA achieved high hit rates of 40%, 20%, and 30%. Notably, for some of the established targets, DrugJEPA identified single-digit nanomolar active molecules, while for entirely new targets, it still offered nanomolar-potency hits. This work represents a pioneering effort in ultra-fast virtual screening of ultra-large chemical libraries, making such screening affordable for conventional drug development programs.

items.title: Lightweight defect detection on mica sheets via focused distillation for industrial measurement
items.abstract: Abstract To address the dual demands of accuracy and efficiency in detecting irregular surface defects on mica sheets, this paper proposes a comprehensive solution that integrates the design of a vision system and a lightweight detection method. First, we build a high-precision automated vision acquisition system to capture mica sheet images in batches and construct a dataset based on the defect characteristics. Next, we build a mica sheet defect detector using Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN), which achieves accurate classification and localization of defects after training on the custom dataset. Finally, we introduce a knowledge distillation framework based onfocused features and responses, transferring the feature extraction and response evaluation capabilities from a high-accuracy, large-capacity model to a lightweight model. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The resulting lightweight model achieves 30.8% mean Average Precision (mAP) with only 28.1M parameters, striking a favorable balance between detection accuracy and efficiency. This provides reliable support for the insulation safety risk assessment of mica sheets.

items.title: High sensitivity temperature sensor based on parallel cascaded microring resonator array
items.abstract: We present a temperature sensor based on a parallel-cascaded microring-resonator (MRR) array on a vertically integrated Si–Si3N4 platform. The lower layer contains ten silicon (Si) microring resonators with the same designed radius, whereas the upper silicon nitride (Si3N4) bus waveguide provides the through-port transmission path. The identical-ring cascade mainly induces coupled-resonator spectral reshaping and multiresonance filtering rather than a conventional Vernier effect based on intentional FSR mismatch. Experimentally, the device exhibits an extinction ratio exceeding 5 dB, an FSR of ∼2.72 nm, and an extracted Q factor of ∼8.13×104 near 1582 nm. Under identical temperature loading from 10°C to 40°C, the tracked array branch shifts by 1.952 nm and yields 64.86 pm/°C. The isolated single-ring reference shifts by 0.936 nm and yields 31.01 pm/°C, corresponding to a 2.09-fold array-to-ring ratio. A direct baseline-normalized overlay between the measured 10°C spectrum and the simulated 0π phase spectrum shows partial agreement in resonance positions and spectral profiles, whereas residual deviations reveal fabrication-induced detuning, coupling nonuniformity and measurement-limited spectral contrast. We demonstrate a promising coupled-resonator approach for high-linearity on-chip temperature sensing.

items.title: Boosting Solar Cell Efficiency Through Plasma-Driven Light Management Strategies: A Review
items.abstract: Background: The optical losses in the form of reflections, parasitic absorption, and scattering limit photovoltaic efficiency. This review examines plasma-assisted surface engineering as an effective tool for improving light management in solar cells. Plasma-based methods, including etching, oxidation, deposition, and texturing, enable precise control of surface morphology and chemistry, lowering reflectance, enhancing light trapping, and passivating defects. Methods: In contrast to wet-chemical or high-temperature processes, plasma processes are dry, low-temperature, scalable, and can be used with silicon, perovskite, thin-film, and organic solar cells, as well as tandem structures. The fundamentals of optical losses are described, along with the principles of radio-frequency (RF), inductively coupled plasma (ICP), microwave, and atmospheric plasma systems and their distinctive advantages for controlling ion and reactive-species generation. Key applications reviewed include black-silicon texturing by ICP reactive-ion etching (ICP-RIE), anti-reflective/passivation coatings by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), and interface activation by atmospheric plasma. Results: Among performance improvements are a reflectance of less than 2%, a photocurrent increase of 10–20%, and longer carrier lifetime. Conclusions: The advantages of plasma compared to lithography and sol–gel processes are in the precision and affordability of the method. The difficulties include damage caused by the processing, uniformity over extensive areas, and environmental stress resistance. Future directions rely on low-temperature plasmas for flexible PV, machine-learning-guided process optimization, and hybrid plasma–laser systems. This synthesis of otherwise fragmented studies is intended to support the implementation of plasma-based methods in next-generation, high-efficiency, and sustainable solar production.

items.title: Beyond Pairwise Polarization: A Statistical Null Model for Structural Balance in Signed Hypergraphs
items.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Abstract Structural balance theory explains polarization through relationships organizing into cohesive, antagonistic factions. Existing statistical tests for the theory rest on pairwise signed graphs, even though many systems it targets, legislative blocs, alliances, coalitions, are group-level phenomena. We introduce a statistical framework for testing structural balance directly on two-sided signed hypergraphs, built from raw group-interaction data. We define the Hyperedge Frustration Index, prove a corrected structure theorem for exact higher-order balance, and construct a degree-and-size-preserving null model for significance testing, correcting two implementation errors along the way. Applied to seventy-five years of UN General Assembly votes, five of fifteen five-year windows survive Benjamini-Hochberg correction at B = 500 replicates: 1946 to 1950, the early Cold War Soviet bloc; 1981 to 1990, two windows of United States isolation; and 2001 to 2010, two windows of a United States-Israel-Pacific bloc. The remaining ten windows, including two decades of decolonization-era voting, show no signal distinguishable from chance. This is our central finding: higher-order balance is real, statistically established across five coherent windows, and genuinely absent elsewhere. Comparing our measure to the standard pairwise pipeline on the same data shows the two track overall trend, Spearman ρ = 0.68, but diverge sharply in substance, agreeing in composition only in 1946 to 1950. A secondary validation on congressional cosponsorship data recovers known party homophily, more strongly once mixing is corrected. The results establish both a validated null-model methodology and a genuine empirical pattern: real historical coalitions detected with statistical rigor, not asserted from optimization alone.

items.title: A Three-Input DC-DC Boost Converter for Grid-Connected Hybrid PV-Wind-Battery Energy Systems
items.venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
items.abstract: The growing penetration of renewable energy sources into modern power networks has intensified the need for compact, efficient, and reliable multi-source power-conversion architectures. This paper presents the design, modeling, and MATLAB/Simulink-based validation of a three-input DC-DC boost converter that simultaneously integrates a photovoltaic (PV) array (105 V, 1.5 kW), a permanent-magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind energy conversion system (80 V, 1.2 kW), and a 48 V/100 Ah lithium-ion battery storage unit onto a single regulated 400 V DC link. Using only four controlled switches and two coupled inductors, the proposed topology replaces three conventional single-input converters, reducing component count by approximately 55% while achieving a peak conversion efficiency of 94.2%. Independent duty-ratio control enables Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) of the PV source, power regulation of the wind source, and bidirectional battery charge/discharge management across three clearly defined operating modes. The regulated DC bus feeds a grid-connected voltage source inverter (VSI) synchronized through a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) and interfaced to the utility through an LCL output filter. Simulation results confirm stable output-voltage regulation (400 V ± 3 V), a total harmonic distortion (THD) of 2.8%, which satisfies the IEEE 519 limit, and a near-unity power factor of 0.997, validating the proposed converter as an efficient and economical solution for grid-connected hybrid renewable energy applications.

items.title: Transformational leadership, sustainability governance, and organizational maturity in higher education institutions: a systematic review toward sustainable energy performance
items.abstract: Universities consume energy at an industrial scale, yet most struggle to translate sustainability commitments into operational change. Three constructs bear on this problem: transformational leadership (TL), sustainability governance, and organizational maturity. Each has its own research tradition, but whether and how they converge in the higher education literature remains unclear. This systematic review maps that convergence. Following PRISMAL 2020, we searched Scopus and Web of Science for work published between 2014 and 2026, identifying 230 records that were screened down to a final corpus of 34 studies for descriptive bibliometric and thematic analysis. Leadership was the most frequently central construct: 50.0% of studies treat it as a focus, followed by governance at 44.1%. Organizational maturity was central in only one study (2.9%). No study in the corpus treated all three constructs as central variables, and none paired leadership with maturity in the absence of governance; these patterns held under both strict (direct-only) and lax (direct-plus-partial) coding. The corpus was overwhelmingly unidimensional: 85.3% of studies addressed a single construct as a central variable. Asia and the Middle East contributed 55.9% of studies; Latin America only 5.9%, with a single study from Ecuador. Six thematic categories emerged, from green TL and PLS-SEM work to German governance frameworks and Latin American case studies. Within the reviewed corpus, two gaps are notable: no study examined how leadership builds organizational maturity for sustainability directly, and no study integrated all three constructs as central variables. Leadership maturity models exist in professional practice but were not identified in HEI sustainability research. Read as a research agenda rather than a settled conclusion, these patterns motivate five propositions oriented toward a Governance and Maturity Model (MGM) for scaling solar energy and efficiency projects on university campuses, with particular attention to Latin American contexts where structured maturity diagnostics appear most needed.

items.title: Thiol−Isocyanate−Epoxy Covalent Adaptable Networks with Versatile Dual-Curing Processing and Tunable Stress Relaxation
items.abstract: Abstract Dual-curing covalent adaptable networks (CANs) provide a powerful platform to tailor thermomechanical properties through controlled network architecture and dynamic bond exchange. In this work, a thiol−isocyanate−epoxy system is employed to construct networks via a sequential photo- and thermally activated curing strategy, enabling precise control over intermediate and final network structures. The resulting materials exhibit composition-dependent stress relaxation behavior governed by the interplay of transthiocarbamoylation and transesterification mechanisms. By systematically varying the stoichiometric ratios, the relative contribution of each dynamic process is tuned, providing insight into structure−dynamics relationships in dual-curing networks. A simplified structural model is evaluated against experimental stress relaxation data, demonstrating its ability to capture key trends while highlighting its limitations in systems involving multiple concurrent exchange mechanisms. This work establishes a framework for the design of dual-curing CANs with tunable relaxation behavior and reprocessing capabilities.

items.title: Real-time conductivity monitoring of industrial lubricating oils using an interdigital electrode sensor
items.abstract: Purpose To effectively monitor quality of lubricating oil, the purpose of this paper is to design a novel conductivity sensor with interdigital electrode (IDE sensor), which can accurately and stably monitor conductivity of lubricating oil. Design/methodology/approach A reliable calibration curve was established by preparing a series of sample blends composed of 100# gear oil and varying concentrations of additives. The operational stability of the sensor was assessed through repeated measurements on the same oil samples. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the developed IDE sensors was validated by direct comparison with standard offline laboratory conductivity measurements. Findings The rigorous calibration confirmed a strong positive correlation between the sensor output voltage and the conductivity of the oil. The sensor demonstrated excellent operational stability, exhibiting only minimal voltage deviations during repeated measurements of identical oil samples. It achieved high accuracy, with relative errors ranging from 1.8% to 9.4% compared to standard offline laboratory conductivity measurements. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the IDE sensor was successfully validated in an industrial environment, where its on-site conductivity readings from in-service gear oil closely aligned with offline diagnostic results. Originality/value The proposed IDE sensor integrates significant stability, accuracy and in-service reliability, representing a meaningful advance in lubricant monitoring technology for engineering applications.

items.title: Perceived persuasion legitimacy of virtual influencers: a dual-pathway model of consumer acceptance and purchase intention
items.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
items.abstract: Purpose Virtual influencers, algorithmically designed brand-controlled personas, enact persuasion without experiential intention, moral agency or accountability. Existing constructs have not captured act-level evaluation of such conduct. This study introduces Perceived Persuasion Legitimacy of Virtual Influencers (PPL-VI), examining associations with willingness to accept influence (WAI) and purchase intention (PI). Design/methodology/approach Study 1 developed PPL-VI through cue mapping, focus groups (N = 30) and expert interviews (N = 10). Study 2 assessed it via a post-exposure survey (N = 878) of Indian social media users, using PLS-SEM with a Type II hierarchical specification. Study 3 (N = 214) was a two-condition experiment. Findings PPL-VI comprises four formative dimensions: Integrity of Persuasion Enactment, Respect for Persuasive Boundaries (RPB), Ethical Treatment of Consumers and Clarity of Responsibility for Persuasion, with RPB carrying the greatest outer weight in Study 2. Value alignment partially mediates the PPL-VI–PI association, procedural fairness the PPL-VI–WAI association and perceived human-likeness modestly moderates both. Study 3 suggests PPL-VI is associated with variance in purchase intention beyond adjacent constructs under lower-legitimacy conditions. Research limitations/implications Study 2 is cross-sectional, so causal inference requires further replication. The India-only, non-probability samples limit generalisability; Study 3 manipulated one dimension. Practical implications Brands may benefit from monitoring boundary restraint and ethical consumer treatment alongside the other dimensions; recommendations are hypothesis-generating and directional rather than prescriptive. Originality/value This study develops and provides initial evidence for a 16-item instrument for act-level legitimacy evaluation in AI-mediated persuasion and proposes an act-level PKT adaptation integrating the Computers as Social Actors paradigm.

items.title: MONTE CARLO-BASED UNCERTAINTY ANALYSIS OF NON-IDEAL BIDIRECTIONAL DC-DC CONVERTER
items.venue: REVUE ROUMAINE DES SCIENCES TECHNIQUES — SÉRIE ÉLECTROTECHNIQUE ET ÉNERGÉTIQUE
items.abstract: Bidirectional DC-DC converters are widely employed in DC bus-based power systems that supply resistive DC loads due to their simple structure and inherent capability for bidirectional power flow. This paper presents a comprehensive Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analysis of a non-ideal bidirectional DC-DC converter operating with a resistive DC load. Inductor and capacitor tolerances, parasitic resistances, and component operating temperature uncertainties are simultaneously randomized to assess their combined impact on DC bus voltage regulation during bidirectional operation. Simulation results confirm that the bidirectional converter maintains stable operation and bounded performance dispersion under parametric uncertainties. The proposed framework provides a robustness-oriented evaluation methodology that complements conventional deterministic analysis for DC bus-interfaced power converters.

items.title: Function-based allocation for recycling and waste-to-energy systems: A unit-process framework for attributional LCA
items.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Providing comparable attributional footprints of multifunctional recycling systems and their products is a long-running and controversial issue in LCA. This study proposes a function-based allocation approach for multi-input–multi-output recycling systems that yields functionally aligned cradle-to-gate footprints for recyclates and explicit footprints for waste-treatment and energy products. We ask how composition-based, function-based allocation can be operationalised in attributional recycling LCAs while respecting ISO 14040/44. Methods We develop a conceptual framework that functionally separates recycling systems into waste treatment (WT) and resource provision, further split into material provision (MP) and energy provision (EP). Based on article-level recyclability factors and the measured composition of the material streams, we derive composition-based recyclable-material shares for each fraction and use them to allocate burdens between WT, MP and EP. Process yields are reported as performance indicators and mass-balance checks, but are not used as allocation keys. Results and discussion A numerical example shows that the proposed allocation yields cradle-to-gate recyclate footprints that predominantly reflect material provision, while burdens for treating non-recyclables are assigned to WT and EP footprints. System inefficiencies (losses of recyclable material) become quantitatively visible and are attributed back to recyclates, creating clear incentives to improve yields and design for recycling. Compared with simple mass allocation and generic end-of-life approaches, the method resolves problems of the known inconsistent allocation approaches, avoids hidden double counting, and maintains the summation rule across recyclates, waste-treatment services and energy outputs. Conclusions The function-based allocation approach enables comparison of recyclate and virgin-material footprints at consistent system boundaries, subject to separate verification of substitutability, and makes the WT service of recycling systems explicitly quantifiable. It can directly support procurement, eco-design, benchmarking and policy instruments that rely on cradle-to-gate footprints for secondary materials, and can be integrated with existing frameworks such as Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) method or Environmental Product Declarations (EPD) programmes. Recommendations: Within recycling systems, the four-step procedure operationalises the physical-relationship allocation permitted under ISO 14044, replacing the interpretive latitude of generic recycled-content approaches with a reproducible, composition-based method that improves cross-study comparability. At the inter-life-cycle level, function-based cradle-to-gate outputs can complement existing frameworks such as the Circular Footprint Formula. Harmonised default data for recyclability and exergy parameters, and extension to chemical recycling, are priorities for future work.

items.title: Experimental investigation of hydrogen solubility in water, NaCl solutions, and deep saline reservoir fluids from the Ketzin site under subsurface conditions
items.abstract: The solubility of hydrogen ( H 2 ) was experimentally determined in pure water, NaCl solutions, and deep reservoir brines from the Ketzin site using a high-pressure autoclave setup. Experiments were conducted at temperatures up to 373.15 K and pressures up to 200 bar, covering conditions relevant for underground hydrogen storage. Hydrogen solubility increases with pressure, whereas temperature effects are comparatively moderate and partly non-monotonic. Measurements in pure water reproduce literature data and confirm the characteristic temperature inversion behavior of hydrogen dissolution. In saline systems, a pronounced salting-out effect reduces hydrogen solubility relative to pure water. This effect becomes stronger in the complex Ketzin brines, where increasing ionic strength and multi-ion composition further suppress the temperature sensitivity of hydrogen dissolution. At reservoir-relevant conditions, only a small fraction of injected hydrogen is expected to dissolve into the formation brine. A key outcome of this work is the generation of the first experimentally determined hydrogen solubility dataset for natural multi-ion reservoir brines. The dataset provides an experimental basis for future thermodynamic and reservoir-scale modeling studies, supports the assessment of dissolution-driven hydrogen losses, and contributes to reducing uncertainties in the evaluation of underground hydrogen storage performance.

items.title: Exercise adaptation and proactive health: an information-theoretic framework based on load entropy
items.abstract: Abstract Exercise is among the most powerful stimuli for promoting health, yet exercise science still prescribes load largely through fixed, population-derived intensity zones that overlook how individuals perceive and adapt to training stimuli. This review develops Proactive Health as a scientific framework in which exercise is the central means of cultivating adaptive capacity and introduces an information-theoretic model – load entropy – to explain why individuals respond differently to the same exercise challenge. Drawing on principles from complexity science, information theory and non-equilibrium thermodynamics, the framework conceptualises health as adaptive capacity rather than the absence of disease and positions entropy as a central organising principle of biological adaptation. Within this view, health is reframed as adaptive capacity rather than the absence of disease, and entropy becomes a central organising principle of biological adaptation: exercise perturbs the system, transiently raises local entropy and informational uncertainty, and thereby triggers the self-organised reorganisation that underlies training adaptation. Building on psychophysics, the load entropy model reconceptualises exercise load not as a purely mechanical scalar but as the perceptual uncertainty an individual experiences in discriminating a stimulus, which peaks at an entropy-defined “effective stimulus” – a hypothesised, individually and momentarily specific threshold of maximal adaptive challenge. We show how this construct connects to established practice such as heart-rate-variability-guided training and load monitoring, and how it could inform personalised exercise prescription, rehabilitation and digital-twin, AI-enabled care. As a conceptual and hypothesis-driven review, the work generates testable hypotheses for personalised exercise prescription, rehabilitation and exercise monitoring and provides a translational framework for proactive, adaptive healthcare.

items.title: Coupled density–viscosity controls in low-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage under heterogeneous conditions
items.abstract: Abstract Aquifer heterogeneity and temperature-dependent fluid properties are key controls on heat transport in aquifer thermal energy storage systems, yet their combined influence on performance reliability in low-temperature doublets remains insufficiently quantified. We evaluate a three-dimensional confined-aquifer model using 50 stochastic hydraulic-conductivity realizations, four density–viscosity coupling schemes, and warm-well injection temperatures ranging from 14 to 30 °C, while the cold-well injection temperature is fixed at 6 °C. Performance is assessed using thermal-recovery percentiles, uncertainty range, and a robustness index that integrates mean performance, variability, and a minimum acceptable recovery threshold. Simulations reveal a pronounced asymmetry between the two wells. Warm-well recovery remains relatively stable across the investigated temperature range, whereas cold-well recovery deteriorates strongly with increasing warm-well injection temperature. The 10th-percentile cold-well thermal recovery decreases from approximately 61% at 14 °C to below 25% at 30 °C, reaching as low as 4.2% when both density and viscosity are treated as temperature dependent, while the corresponding robustness index decreases from approximately 0.8 to below 0.34. This reliability loss is associated with preferential inter-well heat transport in unfavorable heterogeneous realizations, amplified by increased fluid mobility. Within the investigated LT-ATES range, with warm-well injection temperatures not exceeding 30 °C and a maximum warm–cold injection-temperature contrast of 24 °C, temperature-dependent density has only a minor influence on the selected performance indicators. In contrast, neglecting temperature-dependent viscosity can overestimate lower-percentile cold-well recovery and robustness. Regional groundwater flow further reduces recovery at both wells, while increasing well distance mainly improves cold-well reliability by limiting inter-well thermal interference. These results identify the cold well as the reliability-limiting component and show that median recovery alone can mask unfavorable heterogeneous conditions. Lower-percentile and robustness-based metrics therefore provide useful complementary information for reliable low-temperature ATES design in heterogeneous aquifers.
